mappings.note: Who is called a practical idealist: content comprehension of the 'गिन्नी का सोना' section, LO-1. Not LO-2, which would require the author's standpoint to be appraised.
How many are admitted to the tea ceremony (three): a stated detail, LO-1.
What the author means by saying the Japanese have a speed engine in their heads: appraising his figure of speech, which is LO-2's भाषा-शैली की सराहना rather than plain content recall.
The Japanese name for the tea ritual (चा-नो-यू): a stated term, LO-1.
Who gave society its lasting values: content comprehension of the text's claim, LO-1.
Who is always alert: comprehension of the contrast the text draws, LO-1.
What is mixed into gold ornaments (copper): a stated detail that carries the essay's analogy, LO-1.
What pure gold stands for: the text states the equivalence with pure idealism outright, so this is comprehension, LO-1, not an appraisal of the author's craft.
Why the sound of boiling water was so clear to the writer: comprehension of the described silence, LO-1.
Who took the writer to the tea ceremony: a stated detail, LO-1.
What some people call Gandhiji according to the writer: content comprehension, the converse of qid:104417.
What the writer means to inspire through the two episodes: the author's मंतव्य, LO-2, which is the appraisal outcome rather than the content outcome.
Which languages besides Hindi Kelekar wrote in: author biography from the लेखक परिचय. Neither LO reaches outside the prescribed text, so the literature competency is cited.
Kelekar's leanings as a student: author biography, competency level as with qid:104429.
Kelekar's date of birth: author biography, competency level.
The harms of व्यवहारवाद as the essay sets them out: content comprehension, LO-1. LO-2 is reserved for items asking what the writer means to convey overall, as at qid:104428.
Duplicate stem of qid:104424; what pure gold symbolises, stated in the text, LO-1.
What change the writer felt in himself after the tea: comprehension of his described experience, LO-1.
Duplicate stem of qid:104420; the Japanese name for the tea ritual, LO-1.
What pure idealism amounts to in the essay's terms: the writer's central position, so LO-2. Contrast qid:104424, which only asks what the gold stands for.
